title: The Scarecrow Classic
description: It's the 47th annual Scarecrow Classic on Snazzie FM, the harvest contest where every family stakes a stuffed scarecrow in the square. The proud chairman calls in about the streak, a new postal carrier mentions nobody's collected mail on Elm Street since the scarecrows got good, and a longtime resident explains the town has quietly reorganized daily life around not making eye contact with the winners.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight, the square is glowing. It's the 47th annual Scarecrow Classic, the proudest harvest tradition this town has. Marv, you've chaired this contest for decades. Welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Forty-seven years. <p:0.3> Of stuffing dolls and staking them in the dirt. <p:0.3> Just so we're all clear on what we're celebrating.

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: It's a deep honor, Ronnie. Forty-seven years undefeated. <p:0.3> Forty-seven straight blue ribbons. You don't argue with a streak like that, you build a town around it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now THAT'S a Classic. Every family stitching their own champion. <p:0.3> That right there is the soul of this town, Barry.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's a nice ribbon, Marv. I'll give you that. <p:0.3> Quick one, though. Who actually judges these things?

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: We stopped sending judges in eighty-one, Barry. <p:0.3> You don't disqualify a champion for technique. The winner makes itself obvious. It always has.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Hi, yeah, hello. Darnell, I'm the new postal carrier, took the route last month. <p:0.3> So, for the record, I love a parade. I do. <p:0.3> But I cannot deliver to Elm Street.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: A young man learning the lay of the land. Welcome aboard, Darnell.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Thank you. So, for the record, every box on Elm is stuffed full. Nobody's collected mail since, and I'm quoting a sticky note in the truck here, since the scarecrows got good.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Got good. <p:0.3> Marv, what does it mean when a scarecrow gets good?

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: It means it earned its stake, Barry. <p:0.3> A ribbon-grade scarecrow holds its post. Doesn't slump, doesn't fall in a storm. <p:0.3> Elm Street's had the same six champions for six years running.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, hello, dears. Mildred, on Elm. <p:0.3> Don't you fuss about the mail, young man. You just don't look at the winner, that's all. It's only manners.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, Darnell? Pure small-town etiquette. You don't gawk at a champion. <p:0.3> That's just respect, Barry.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: So, for the record, the route map has a note on it too. <p:0.3> Elm Street residents are advised to walk backwards past the square. <p:0.3> Who advised that?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: We all just sort of started, dear. Years ago. <p:0.3> It's easier on the neck than keeping your eyes down the whole walk. You just don't look at the winner.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: An entire street walks BACKWARDS, Ronnie. <p:0.3> That is not etiquette. That is the opposite of etiquette.

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: It's reverence, Barry. <p:0.3> You measure a town by how it carries itself past greatness. Forty-seven ribbons of greatness.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Okay, so, for the record, the curtains. <p:0.3> Every house on Elm faces away from the square. The windows are all on the wrong side. Who builds a house backwards?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: We turned the parlors around in the spring, dear. As a group. <p:0.3> It's nicer not to have the square watching you have your tea. You just don't look at the winner.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: They re-pointed their HOUSES, Ronnie! <p:0.3> Marv, normal scarecrows do not require a town to look away from them!

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: A champion commands the room, Barry. <p:0.3> You don't disqualify a winner just because folks can't hold its gaze.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's heritage you can't fake. A whole street, redesigned around respect. <p:0.3> Now THAT'S a Classic.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: So, for the record, Marv, real fast. <p:0.3> The note says six champions on Elm. <p:0.3> But I counted seven scarecrows in the square tonight. Who's the seventh?

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: Seven? <p:0.3> Son, we only registered six entries this year.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Then what's the SEVENTH one, Marv?!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Oh, no. <p:0.3> Young man, where are you standing right now?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Front of the square, by the new one. <p:0.3> It's wearing a postal cap. <p:0.3> And I am... I'm looking right at it.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Don't look at the winner, dear!

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: Ribbon!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Backwards!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: [surprise-yo] It's wearing my CAP!

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: Folks, we have a result. <p:0.3> The new entry takes first. Forty-eight years undefeated.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Marv, do NOT give it a ribbon!

lines.speaker: caller-marv
lines.text: Already pinned, Barry. <p:0.3> And I'm penciling next year's entry in now, under the name Darnell. You don't break up a winning streak.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Why is it... why is it holding still the exact way I'm holding still?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Forty-seven years undefeated. <p:0.3> Barry, you don't argue with a streak like that. <p:0.3> Darnell, whatever you do down there... don't look at the winner.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: ...Too late, dear.
